body_markdown:
The mighty, 1064-horsepower[Aston Martin Valhalla](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/aston-martin-valhalla-1079-hp-of-driving-heaven/) now doubles as a very, very fancy hair dryer. Unveiled online ahead of its public debut in Las Vegas, the new Valhalla Spider is the fastest open-top car the British brand has ever made. The Spider is powered by a gasoline-electric hybrid drivetrain, and it can hit its top speed of over 210 mph regardless of whether the roof panel is on or off.


Buyers can choose between two removable roof panels, and how fast you can go in the Spider depends on which panel you pick. Stick with the standard cloth top, which comes in black, and you’ll be limited to 124 mph when driving with the roof on. Take the cloth panel off, and you’ll be able to reach the same 217-mph top speed as the Valhalla coupe. Alternatively, Aston Martin offers a carbon-fiber hard top that lets the Valhalla Spider max out at 217 mph regardless of whether the panel is on or off.


Inside, the Spider stands out from the[Valhalla coupe](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cyMxh5prL8s) with new Touring seats that make the cabin easier to get in and out of, a folding wind deflector that can be stored when not in use, and dihedral doors modified for smoother operation. Aston notes that the carbon-fiber seats from the Valhalla coupe can be swapped for the Touring seats as a no-cost option for buyers who prioritize support over comfort.

Aston Martin didn’t make any mechanical modifications. Power for the Spider comes from a gasoline-electric hybrid drivetrain that consists of a twin-turbocharged, 4.0-liter V-8 engine with a flat-plane crankshaft, a pair of electric motors (one for each front wheel), a third electric motor integrated into the eight-speed automatic transmission, and a 6.1-kilowatt-hour battery. The total output checks in at 1064 horsepower and 811 pound-feet of torque. Translating the power of that intricate setup to the ground requires a great deal of technology, but Aston Martin stresses that its engineers calibrated the drivetrain to deliver a driving experience that’s “organic and natural.”


The brand also revised the active aerodynamics and the Electronic Stability Programme (ESP) to ensure the Spider remains equally balanced with the roof on or off. The car automatically adjusts its front and rear downforce to maximize grip or reduce drag, depending on the driving conditions and on the driving mode. While it was designed primarily as a road car, the Valhalla Spider sounds engaging on a track. We don’t know what effect (if any) the removable roof has on weight, but the Spider is built around a version of the coupe’s carbon-fiber tub.


The new Aston Martin Valhalla Spider will make its public debut this weekend at the Concours at Wynn Las Vegas. Deliveries will begin in the third quarter of 2027. Pricing hasn’t been announced, but keep in mind that the Valhalla coupe carries a base price of a little over $1 million before options. Odds are the Spider model will cost even more.
